custom.useExample: Button that fills the definition box with a sample agent definition

install.confirm: Button that starts downloading the agent bridge
install.installing: Busy label on the install button while the bridge downloads
install.locationLabel: Row label for the folder the bridge is installed into
install.packageLabel: Row label for the package name of the bridge being installed

registry.register: Button that registers a registry entry as an available agent
registry.registered: Disabled button state meaning this agent is already registered
registry.search: Button that submits the ACP registry search query
registry.searching: Busy label on the registry search button while the search runs

file.discard: Button that throws away unsaved edits and re-reads the approvals file
file.reload: Button that re-reads the approvals file from disk when nothing is edited
file.saving: Busy label on the save button while the approvals file is written

project.allowed: Badge meaning this tool always runs without asking in this project
project.denied: Badge meaning this tool is always refused in this project

customProvider.baseUrlPlaceholder: Example API endpoint. Keep the URL verbatim.
customProvider.idLabel: Short machine readable identifier for a user added provider
customProvider.idPlaceholder: Example identifier. Keep it lowercase ASCII letters only.
customProvider.namePlaceholder: Example display name for a fictional company
customProvider.submitAdd: Button that creates the new provider

instructions.saved: Confirmation shown beside the button after custom instructions are saved

models.custom: Badge on a model the user typed in by hand rather than one the provider listed

metadata.unknownDate: Substituted for a date that could not be read, inside "Model data updated {{date}}"

models.refresh: Fetch the provider's current model list again
models.restore: Put this provider's built-in models back into the list
models.title: Heading over the list of AI models available from one provider

personas.addStarter: Button that adds one suggested persona to the user's personas

colors.forest: Color name for a persona swatch, light to dark green
colors.grape: Color name for a persona swatch, purple to violet
colors.ocean: Color name for a persona swatch, light to dark blue
colors.slate: Color name for a persona swatch, grey
colors.sunset: Color name for a persona swatch, orange to red

form.color: Field label for the persona color picker
form.create: Button that saves a new persona
form.instructions: Field label for the persona prompt text area
form.namePlaceholder: Example persona name shown as placeholder text in the name field

badge.connected: A remote provider has a working API key saved
badge.notRunning: A locally installed model server is not answering
badge.running: A locally installed model server is up and answering

providers.docs: Link to a provider's own documentation website
providers.getKey: Link that opens the provider's signup page where the user creates an API key
providers.modelLabel: Label beside a dropdown that selects which AI model to use

ollama.active: This model is the one currently in use
ollama.check: Button that probes the local machine for a running Ollama server
ollama.disconnect: Forget the saved Ollama host and stop using it
ollama.noModels: Keep the shell command ollama pull llama3.2 verbatim.
ollama.recheck: Button that probes for Ollama again after the first attempt
ollama.setupSteps: Numbered setup instructions. Keep ollama.com, the shell commands ollama serve and ollama pull llama3.2, and the numbers verbatim.

reset.sectionName: The name of this settings section, shown inside the sentence "Reset <name> settings?"

tabs.agents: Command line coding agents such as Claude Code, not AI personas
tabs.skills: Reusable instruction bundles the assistant can load, a product feature name

catalog.install: Button that downloads and installs a catalog skill.
catalog.refresh: Button that re-fetches the skill catalog from the network.
catalog.uninstall: Button that deletes an installed catalog skill.
catalog.update: Button that installs a newer version of an installed catalog skill.

editor.instructions: Field label for the body of SKILL.md, the steps the assistant follows.
editor.submitCreate: Button that creates the new skill.

groups.shelf: Heading over skills installed from the downloadable domain catalog.
groups.user: Heading over skills the user wrote themselves.

skills.invalidBadge: Badge on a skill whose SKILL.md failed validation.

phases.authoring: Drafting phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.communication: Communication phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.figures: Figure preparation phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.research: Research phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.review: Reviewing phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.submission: Submission phase of a writing project, a group heading for skills.
phases.tooling: Tooling and utility skills, a group heading.

source.added: Badge on a skill the user added from a folder on their computer.
source.bundled: Badge on a skill that ships inside the app.
source.catalog: Badge on a skill downloaded from the domain catalog.

skills.updateAction: Button that replaces an installed skill with a newer bundled version.
skills.useDeviceSetting: Button that clears a per-project override so the skill follows the device-wide setting.

bgPattern.grid: Background pattern made of grid lines.

dock.bottom: Screen edge where the home dock sits, along the bottom.
dock.left: Screen edge where the home dock sits, on the left.
dock.right: Screen edge where the home dock sits, on the right.

theme.label: Heading for the light, dark, and system theme choice.

tokens.accent: Label for the hover and highlight surface color token.
tokens.card: Label for the panel surface color token.
tokens.destructive: Label for the destructive or error color token.
tokens.foreground: Label for the main text color token.
tokens.input: Label for the color token used on input field borders.
tokens.muted: Label for the low emphasis surface color token.
tokens.popover: Label for the floating popover surface color token.
tokens.primary: Label for the primary action color token.
tokens.ring: Label for the color token used on the keyboard focus ring.
tokens.secondary: Label for the secondary surface color token.

homeView.grid: Library layout that arranges projects as a grid of cards.
homeView.list: Library layout that arranges projects as rows in a list.

appearance.sectionName: Name of the Appearance settings section, used inside the reset confirmation sentence.

tabs.app: Tab label for settings that affect the whole application window.
tabs.editor: Tab label for source editor settings.
tabs.files: Tab label for project and file tree settings.
tabs.pdf: Tab label for PDF preview settings.

colors.background: Label for the terminal background color swatch.
colors.cursor: Label for the terminal cursor color swatch.
colors.foreground: Label for the terminal text color swatch.

cursorStyle.bar: Terminal cursor drawn as a thin vertical bar.
cursorStyle.block: Terminal cursor drawn as a filled rectangle.
cursorStyle.underline: Terminal cursor drawn as a line under the character.

citations.connected: Badge showing that a credential is stored for this search source.

openAlex.emailPlaceholder: A literal example address. Keep you@example.com unchanged.

serper.docsLink: Link text. Serper is a product name, keep it unchanged.

citations.title: Name of the Oleafly feature that searches scholarly databases.

cite.apa: Link text. Cite this repository is the name of a GitHub feature, keep it recognizable.
cite.copyBibtex: Button that copies the BibTeX entry to the clipboard.
cite.description: Keep the file extension .bib and the citation key oleafly inside the tags verbatim.

actions.allDownloaded: Disabled button state once every item is already downloaded.
actions.download: Button that starts downloading one item.
actions.downloadAll: Button that downloads every item in the list.

lato.label: Font family name. Keep verbatim in every language.

ptsans.label: Font family name. Keep verbatim in every language.

ptserif.label: Font family name. Keep verbatim in every language.

downloads.progress: {{label}} is the name of the asset being fetched, supplied by the backend.

size.kilobytes: {{value}} is an already formatted number. KB is the unit symbol, keep it verbatim.
size.megabytes: {{value}} is an already formatted number. MB is the unit symbol, keep it verbatim.

tabs.fonts: Tab label for downloadable font packs.
tabs.templates: Tab label for downloadable document template packs.

distributions.rowTooltip: {{tools}} is a list of TeX tool names such as "latexmk and tlmgr". {{binDir}} is a file system path. Keep both verbatim.

engine.latexmkMissing: Warning badge shown when the latexmk binary is not present on the machine. Keep latexmk verbatim.

badge.breaks: Badge on a package that prevents tagged accessible PDF output.
badge.caution: Badge on a package that may not produce cleanly tagged accessible PDFs.

packages.heading: Heading over the list of installable LaTeX packages.
packages.includedIn: {{package}} is a TeX Live package name. Keep it verbatim.
packages.search: Button that queries the TeX Live package repository. Keep TeX Live verbatim.

tree.both: Fragmentless phrase shown as a badge: the package is installed in both the system TeX tree and the user's personal tree.
tree.system: Badge: the package is installed in the machine-wide TeX tree.
tree.user: Badge: the package is installed in the user's personal TeX tree.

error.withDetail: Joins a failure sentence with the raw tlmgr output that explains it

engine.sectionName: Name of the Engines settings section. Also used inside the reset confirmation sentence "Reset {{sectionName}} settings?".

account.connected: Status shown under the avatar when an account is linked but has no display name. Not an action.
account.disconnect: Button that signs the app out of the linked GitHub account.
account.handle: The connected GitHub account handle. Keep the @ prefix and the placeholder verbatim.

advanced.connect: Button that signs in with the personal access token the user pasted.
advanced.toggle: Discloses the fallback sign-in route that uses a personal access token.
advanced.tokenPlaceholder: Example prefix of a GitHub personal access token. Keep it verbatim.

github.connect: Button that starts the GitHub sign-in flow.

device.openGithub: Button that opens the GitHub device authorization page in the browser.
device.waiting: Status shown while the app polls GitHub for the user to finish authorizing.

actions.connect: Button that stores the API key the user pasted and links the account.
actions.disconnect: Button that deletes the stored API key and unlinks the account.

cookies.action: Button label. Starts the browser cookie import.
cookies.hostnamePlaceholder: A literal example hostname. Keep example.com unchanged.
cookies.review: Button that moves from choosing a profile to the confirmation step.

status.available: This browser profile can be read right now.
status.comingSoon: Support for this browser is not implemented yet.
status.noCookieStore: The browser is installed but has no readable cookie database.
status.notInstalled: The browser is not installed on this machine.

cookies.tryAgain: Button that repeats the failed browser detection.

duplicates.legend: Heading for the choice of what to do when an imported server has the same name as an existing one

summary.commandFallback: Shown in place of an executable name when the imported command is empty

registry.version: A version number prefixed with a lowercase v, for example v1.2.3

port.label: A network port number, not a verb and not a software port

token.hide: Button that hides the secret token again
token.regenerate: Button that issues a new secret token and invalidates the old one
token.reveal: Button that shows the hidden secret token on screen

card.validate: Button that runs a connection check against one server

editor.argsLabel: Command line arguments passed to the executable, not points in a debate
editor.commandLabel: The executable to run, for example npx
editor.formView: Segment that switches the editor to the field by field form, as opposed to raw JSON
editor.jsonView: Segment that switches the editor to raw JSON. Keep the word JSON verbatim

pairs.storedValuePlaceholder: Placeholder shown when a secret is already saved and stays hidden
pairs.valuePlaceholder: Placeholder for the value half of a name and value pair

editor.transportLegend: How the app talks to the server, either a local command or a remote URL

status.checking: Badge showing that a check of the server is in progress
status.connected: Badge showing that the server responded to a check
status.error: Badge showing that the last check of the server failed

clear.confirm: Button that empties the dictionary of ignored words.
clear.suppressedConfirm: Button that brings dismissed grammar findings back into view.

dismissed.showAgain: Button that un-dismisses every grammar finding hidden in this project.

profileRules.example: Prefix on a sample of what a grammar rule would flag. {{example}} is rule output and stays in English.

reset.sectionName: Name of this settings section, used inside the sentence "Reset <name> settings?".

tabs.global: Tab label for dictionary words that apply to every project.
tabs.projects: Tab label for dictionary words that apply to one project only.

reset.button: Button that restores one settings section to its shipped defaults.
reset.confirmDescription: Body of the confirmation dialog. {{sectionName}} is the name of the settings section.
reset.confirmTitle: Title of the confirmation dialog. {{sectionName}} is the name of the settings section.
reset.description: Sentence under the heading. {{sectionName}} is the name of the settings section, for example Appearance.
reset.label: Heading of the row that resets one settings section.

application.recording: Label on the key box while the app waits for the user to press a key combination.

labels.redo: Redoes the edit that was just undone.

categories.codeIntelligence: Group heading for go to definition, find references and rename, features a language server provides.
categories.editor: Group heading for shortcuts the text editor handles.
categories.pdf: Group heading for shortcuts in the compiled document preview. Keep PDF verbatim.

error.reserved: {{shortcut}} is the name of an operating system command, for example Copy or Paste.

reset.sectionName: Name of this settings section, used inside the sentence "Reset <name> settings?".

tabs.application: Tab label for shortcuts the user can rebind, as opposed to editor shortcuts.
